top_issues: Balance composition legend (on-chain/reserve/secured/hub promise) requires reading the colored key; four bars on one axis with close green/teal hues are not self-evident to a first-timer.
The 'Instant: send up to $182.99, receive up to $23.30' line under the balance is small, muted and sits far from the big number, so the credit-capacity concept is easy to miss.
Recent activity row timestamps are tiny; the left/right number alignment is clean but time and status can be skimmed past.
fixes: Add an inline 'What do these colors mean?' tooltip or one-line caption anchored to the bar legend.
Promote the 'Instant' capability line to a labeled, brighter callout directly under the total (e.g. 'You can pay up to $182.99 right now').
Bump timestamp/status font-size one step and add a subhead 'TODAY' grouping so recent rows scan faster.

top_issues: Route list repeats 'You send 25.00' on every row, adding noise; the fee + route + before/after panels pile three views of the same settlement onto one screen.
The H1 'Your account with H1' before/after panel duplicates the route fee info, increasing cognitive load for the same decision.
'Delivery: Instant' with a 'Change' control is ambiguous about what is actually changeable (delivery vs route).
fixes: Collapse the account before/after panel into a single line under the amount, and keep route rows to one each with fee only.
Move 'Change' next to the route selector and rename to 'Route options' so delivery/route split is clear.
Highlight the selected route row with a stronger border and show 'You send 25.00' once, not per row.

top_issues: The proof hash is displayed but there is no visible 'share/export evidence' affordance, so forwarding a receipt requires manual copy.
'Copy receipt' gives no confirmation state that the copy succeeded.
The dimmed background shows the updated balance, which is good, but the receipt cannot be re-opened from Activity without re-navigating.
fixes: Add a 'Copy evidence bundle' secondary action and a transient 'Copied' confirmation on the Copy receipt button.
Add a share icon that exports a portable receipt (frame, proof, hash) rather than relying on manual selection.
Make the receipt tappable from the Activity row so it can be revisited without re-doing the flow.

top_issues: No dedicated invoice builder: amount is optional, and there are no currency, memo, invoice-number or due-date fields — only a generic QR plus note.
'Capacity 45.50 via H1' and 'Prepare incoming account' are inbound-capacity jargon that a first-timer cannot parse.
The large white QR card breaks the dark theme contrast balance, drawing the eye away from the action buttons.
fixes: Add an invoice mode: required amount, currency selector, memo, invoice number, and a 'Copy invoice' that carries all fields.
Rename 'Prepare incoming account' to 'Where should the money arrive?' and add a one-line 'This is how much can arrive right now.'
Tone the QR panel to a dark card with a white QR inset so it does not dominate the layout.

top_issues: 'Prepare to receive' pushes a 100%/0% collateral slider and 'Accept it as credit instead' — a heavy credit concept into a simple swap, with an alarming red 'Prepare incoming capacity before swapping' warning.
The order book has no depth axis; only price + size are shown, so Anya cannot judge liquidity depth at a glance.
The 'You receive 0.039992 WETH' value is visually small relative to 'You pay 100', understating the output.
fixes: Default swap to credit and make the collateral chooser collapsible; replace the red warning with a neutral 'This may reduce how much you can receive.'
Add a depth bar or cumulative size column to the book so liquidity depth is readable.
Enlarge the 'You receive' figure to match the pay amount scale and show an estimated USD value inline.

top_issues: The legend chips (collateral/at risk/you owe/credit room/in flight) use tiny colored dots that are hard to tell apart, and the multi-segment bar requires going back to the legend.
'They owe you +70.00' is the headline, but the relationship between 'Your credit line to them 115.50' and 'Collateral 60.00' is not connected visually.
'ou owe them' vs 'they owe you' wording in the legend is subtle and easy to misread at small sizes.
fixes: Replace legend dots with larger labeled swatches and repeat the color meaning directly under the bar.
Draw a small connector or formula line linking credit line, collateral, and the resulting 'at risk' figure.
Use explicit words 'You owe' / 'They owe' as full labels, not abbreviations.

top_issues: No time-range or date grouping beyond 'TODAY', so history depth and navigation are unclear for a long-running account.
Detail panel repeats some list row data, and there is no search to find a specific frame or proof.
Filter chips (All/Payments/Swaps/Settlement/Accounts) are visible but there is no count per filter to guide expectation.
fixes: Add date groups (TODAY/YESTERDAY/THIS MONTH) plus a date-range filter for the account.
Add a search box keyed to counterparty, hash, or frame number.
Show a movement count inside each filter chip.

top_issues: This screenshot is visually identical to 07-activity.png, so the set does not demonstrate a distinct drill-in navigation state beyond the always-on side panel.
The right panel is dense with small labels (To/Via/Frame/Time/Proof/Frames) that need more spacing to read at a glance.
The 'From your runtime's committed frames' note is helpful but the '2 committed entries' count is not expandable to show those entries.
fixes: Provide a separate drill-in screen where the left list is collapsed and the detail takes focus, to prove navigation states.
Increase spacing and font size in the detail grid; keep mono values but give labels more breathing room.
Make '2 committed entries' clickable to reveal the underlying frame hashes inline.

top_issues: Very dense: many controls visible at once, and the global On-chain/Reserve/Accounts toggles could disable core functionality without strong contextual warning.
The '1px = $1' bar-scale demo is delightful but the Auto → $1 slider relationship requires a second read to grasp.
'Reveal recovery phrase' appears on the same page as less-sensitive controls, which that may understate the danger of that action.
fixes: Group settings into collapsible sections and add a confirmation modal with explicit warning when a toggles off On-chain/Reserve/Accounts.
Label the bar-scale demo 'What one pixel of bar is worth' and animate the slider change between Auto and fixed values.
Pull 'Reveal recovery phrase' into a separate, gated Danger zone section with a password/confirmation step.

top_issues: 'Move' between Wallet/Reserve/Account layers is a self-custody concept a first-timer will not understand from the three cards alone.
Only the Account card is selected; the Wallet and Reserve cards are dim but tappable with no explanation of the tradeoff.
'Add to batch' is vague — no context on what batching buys (better fee, timing) or how to review it later.
fixes: Add a one-line 'What is Move?' explainer: 'Move your own money between an on-chain wallet, reserve, and instant account.'
Show a short benefit/hint under each From/To card when selected (e.g. 'Instant account = spend right now').
Explain batching: 'Batch to combine moves and save on fees' and link to the pending batch view.

top_issues: Navigation cards (Sovereignty/Move/Assets/Lending/Ownership) have small icons and no priority; there is no obvious primary action for a returning user.
'WHERE YOUR MONEY STANDS' is strong but the green/violet legend is only in the caption text; there is no visual key next to the numbers.
'Needs attention: Nothing waiting on you' is reassuring but rendered at low contrast, so the reassurance can be missed.
fixes: Order the cards by frequency of use and add a one-word action verb under each title (e.g. 'Sovereignty — see what is enforceable').
Add a small green/violet legend next to the 'Where your money stands' totals.
Raise contrast on 'Nothing waiting on you' and add a green check icon to make the reassurance visible.

top_issues: On-chain balances are all 0.00 — the panel is mostly empty and reads as unfinished against the rich Account/Reserve views.
The Faucet panel stacks four CTAs (Accept as credit, Receive from H1, to on-chain wallet, gas) creating decision fatigue, and it is clearly a testnet-only feature with no production disclaimer.
The 'Prepare to receive' collateral/credit slider reappears, duplicating a heavy concept that does not belong in a simple asset overview.
fixes: Show a positive empty state ('No funds on-chain yet — move some from your reserve') instead of a wall of zeros.
Collapse the faucet CTAs into a single primary 'Request test funds' plus a secondary 'Learn how this works' link.
Duplicate the credit/collateral chooser issue from Swap — remove it from Assets or collapse to a simple 'Use credit' toggle.

top_issues: 'Interest 100 bps' is rendered as '= 100% per term', which is numerically misleading — 100 bps is 1%, and 'per term' vs annualized is not clarified; this is the single most trust-damaging element in the whole set.
The pool summary (Available/Borrowed/Active principal) is all 0.00, so there is no demonstration of a live pool.
There is no 'Borrow' state visible and no rate history, so the terms cannot be judged against alternatives.
fixes: Show '1% (100 bps) per term' and state the term clearly (e.g. 'per 1-day term'), plus an annualized equivalent.
Populate a sample live pool state or show a 'No offers yet' empty state with a clear explanation.
Add a rate-history sparkline or a 'typical offer' benchmark so the term is comparable.

top_issues: The screen is very sparse — a large empty right region that makes the panel feel unfinished.
'Kind: Lazy (hash of its board)' is unexplained jargon; most non-hub users will not know what a lazy entity is.
There are no visible actions to change the threshold or signers, so the board cannot be edited from here.
fixes: Fill the empty region with an explainer card: 'What a lazy entity is and why the hash of the board is the identity.'
Replace 'Lazy (hash of its board)' with a labeled term and a tooltip/expand for detail.
Add 'Change threshold' and 'Add signer' actions so the board is actually manageable.

top_issues: 'Enforceable right now $40.00' is a brilliant headline, but the neighboring 'Hub promise $97.99' at-risk figure can leave a user unsure what the headline actually covers.
Keys section shows signer/entity hashes with no copy affordance.
'Can dispute without asking 1 of 1' — the 'without asking' phrasing is ambiguous about whether a human is in the loop.
fixes: Add a one-line subtitle under the number: 'This is covered by on-chain or collateral; the rest is a hub's promise.'
Add copy buttons beside the Signer and Entity hashes.
Rephrase to 'Can dispute without a co-signer (1 of 1)' so the authority model is unambiguous.

top_issues: Extremely dense: the lane table has ~9 columns and the font is small, so on many screens it will require horizontal scrolling and is hard to scan.
The 'at risk' column is a single number with no color-weight in-cell indication, forcing users to correlate with the tiny legend.
Recent feed and book column compete for vertical space and can overlap on narrower widths.
fixes: Give the lane table a minimum readable width and allow sticky first columns so position rows stay visible on scroll.
Add a color-weighted 'at risk' cell (e.g. a small violet bar) so risk reads without the legend.
Separate the Recent feed into its own scrollable panel below, or into a tab, so the book and table never overlap.

top_issues: Action descriptions use small muted text that is hard to read against the dark backdrop.
No 'recent' or contextual actions are surfaced at the top of the palette, so it does not adapt to the current task.
The described dimmed backdrop is the dense Desk view, which remains busy even when dimmed.
fixes: Increase description contrast and font size one step.
Add a 'Recent' section at the top showing the last few actions for the current context.
Dim the backdrop more aggressively (lower opacity/radius) so the palette is the sole focus.

overall.verdict: The desktop-dark set is a cohesive, premium wallet with a genuinely differentiated 'one absolute scale' data language and a strong 'enforceable vs promised' trust framing that most competitors lack. The main drags are jargon density on the balance/composition legend, a thin invoicing story, and the complete absence of a mobile variant in the set, which keeps several personas (Maya, Sofia, Lena) from fully landing.
priority_fixes: Add an on-demand plain-language explainer (tooltip/inline 'What do these colors mean?') to the Home bar-scale legend so first-timers do not have to infer green/violet/purple semantics (helps Maya, Tomasz, Dmitri, Marcus).

Turn Receive into a real invoice builder with required amount, currency, memo, invoice number, and a shareable proof-of-request link, so Sofia and Maya can send a professional invoice instead of a bare QR (04).
Make the Swap 'Prepare to receive' collateral/credit chooser optional and non-blocking: default to credit, remove the red 'Prepare incoming capacity' warning, explain collateral only on expand (05).
Add an explicit cross-chain Move/Bridge screen with an upfront fee and time-to-settle breakdown so Fatima sees the full cost and route before confirming (10, 05, 12).
Reduce Desk density: give the lane table a minimum readable width and surface 'at risk' as a color-weighted in-cell bar instead of relying on the tiny legend, for Marcus and Ravi (16).

'Prepare incoming account' and 'capacity' language on 04-receive
Collateral/credit chooser on 12-assets

personas.name: Tomasz

Legend chips too small to distinguish on 06

Collateral/credit slider forced into the swap flow on 05
Desk table too dense on 16-desk

personas.name: Ravi

Evidence-bundle save is a manual on-device action on 15-sovereignty

personas.name: Sofia

personas.name: Kenji

Pay screen on 02-pay is a multi-field form, not a single-tap quick-pay
No evidence of one-hand interaction or fast checkout

'Move' on 10-move is wallet/reserve/account, not chain-to-chain
